changes.what: s3t_prefix.py: a fresh bucket prefix for every test
changes.reason: upstream's autouse fixture empties every bucket of one prefix before each test, so one bucket an engine cannot delete errors every later test of the worker; with a prefix per test it is charged to the test that made it

changes.what: requirements.lock: the versions installed into the run's venv
changes.reason: the pinned commit's requirements.txt pins ranges; a lock makes two runs of one engine, and of an engine against its own recording, the same install

changes.what: s3t_report.py: one JSON line per test report, written as each phase ends
changes.reason: pytest writes its junit report when the session ends, which a run cut at the suite's budget never reaches; a line per report survives the cut, so the cases that answered are read and the ones that never reported are the budget's and not the engine's

changes.what: pytest --timeout 600: one test's own budget, fixed for every run
changes.reason: a test that hangs on an engine is that case's failure within ten minutes, and never the whole run's budget: the timeout is ours and does not move with whichever case asked for the run

changes.what: s3t_identity.py: a test asking for a user the row has not got is a skip
changes.reason: s3-tests' get_alt_*() and get_tenant_*() name the conf's second users, and a row with one key pair or no tenants has none: the conf carries a placeholder instead of the main pair, and every getter of that user raises a skip the harness reads as the dependency on the check that measures the identity, instead of running the test as the main user and charging the engine
RGW extensions or AWS IAM, out of the S3 data-plane claim this protocol measures
